        Here is the patch content:
        From df8b13a1b23356d01dfc4647a5629cdb0f4ce566 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shiraz Saleem <shiraz.saleem@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Dec 2017 09:46:59 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] i40iw: Fix sequence number for the first partial FPDU

Partial FPDU processing is broken as the sequence number
for the first partial FPDU is wrong due to incorrect
Q2 buffer offset. The offset should be 64 rather than 16.

Fixes: 786c6adb3a94 ("i40iw: add puda code")
Signed-off-by: Shiraz Saleem <shiraz.saleem@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>
---
 drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_d.h    | 1 +
 drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_puda.c | 2 +-
 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_d.h b/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_d.h
index 65ec39e3746b..b8565872d744 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_d.h
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_d.h
@@ -97,6 +97,7 @@
 #define RDMA_OPCODE_MASK        0x0f
 #define RDMA_READ_REQ_OPCODE    1
 #define Q2_BAD_FRAME_OFFSET     72
+#define Q2_FPSN_OFFSET          64
 #define CQE_MAJOR_DRV           0x8000
 
 #define I40IW_TERM_SENT 0x01
diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_puda.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_puda.c
index 796a815b53fd..f64b6700f43f 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_puda.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/i40iw/i40iw_puda.c
@@ -1378,7 +1378,7 @@ static void i40iw_ieq_handle_exception(struct i40iw_puda_rsrc *ieq,
 	u32 *hw_host_ctx = (u32 *)qp->hw_host_ctx;
 	u32 rcv_wnd = hw_host_ctx[23];
 	/* first partial seq # in q2 */
-	u32 fps = qp->q2_buf[16];
+	u32 fps = *(u32 *)(qp->q2_buf + Q2_FPSN_OFFSET);
 	struct list_head *rxlist = &pfpdu->rxlist;
 	struct list_head *plist;
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug was an incorrect buffer offset used to retrieve the sequence number for the first partial Frame Protocol Data Unit (FPDU). The code was originally using an offset of 16, which did not point to the correct location in the buffer, leading to an incorrect sequence number being processed. The fix involved changing the offset to 64, which correctly points to the intended location in the buffer for the first partial FPDU's sequence number.

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug was an incorrect buffer offset used to retrieve the sequence number for the first partial Frame Protocol Data Unit (FPDU). The code was originally using an offset of 16, which did not point to the correct location in the buffer, leading to an incorrect sequence number being processed. The fix involved changing the offset to 64, which correctly points to the intended location in the buffer for the first partial FPDU's sequence number.
